Each ommatidium is composed of three cells: one receptor cell forming a ciliary receptive and pigment segment, two cells surrounding an extracellular lens (crystalline cone). blocks.text: In annelids most there are usually two fluid systems, the coclom, and the circulatory system, and both (if present) are involved in the excretion of waste products. To achieve this excretion, there must be ducts to the exterior and these are generally referred to as nephridia, Two different kinds of filtration nephridia are described in Annelida: protonephridia and metanephridia. During the development of an annelid, larval protonephridia generally precede segmentally arranged metanephridia. The first pair of larval protonephridia that develop also called are head-kidneys (Hatschek, 1878).
